comparisons.objective: Seal a preloaded carton by closing four flaps, applying and cutting one connected strip from an ordinary tape roll, and leaving the adhesive seal retained; candidate instead separates loose ceramic media from washers through a screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tape payout, thin-ribbon handling, pressure-dependent adhesion, flap folding, cutting, and tool parking versus bimanual screen lifting, load sharing, controlled agitation, selective aperture passage, and support reseating.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires flap closure within 5°, specified seam/end-wrap bond coverage, a detached strip, parked tools, and a 2 s released hold; candidate requires ≥98% media recovery, total washer retention, supported screen, 60 mm hand clearance, and a 3 s dwell, with spill/passage/damage failures. No material rubric detail is missing for comparison.
comparisons.reason: The tested abilities differ materially: creating and retaining an adhesive carton seal does not test selective many-body separation through physical apertures.

comparisons.objective: Turn over a taped carton, cut its bottom seam and end folds, open four flaps, and collapse the intact carton flat; candidate instead sifts ceramic media from retained steel washers and reseats the screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: Carton turnover, guarded cutting, outward flap articulation, and structural collapse versus two-tab grasping, shared-load screen orientation, force-limited agitation, selective passage, and precise two-support replacement.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires measured upright-to-inverted turnover, complete cut coverage, all bottom flaps opened ≥150°, eight flaps coplanar within 15°, a ≤24 mm flat slab, and a 1 s clear-hand hold; candidate grades recovered mass and washer retention plus supported release for 3 s. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve bimanual orientation control, the record tests cutting and articulated carton flattening, not size-selective many-body separation through apertures.

comparisons.objective: Dry all layers of long articulated hair evenly with a handheld dryer while the mannequin head remains fixed; candidate performs rigid-body media/workpiece separation with a manual screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: Airflow positioning, thermal/moisture exposure, occlusion management, flexible-lock manipulation, and dryer operation versus bimanual rigid-screen load sharing, agitation, aperture passage, retention, and reseating.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires every one of 960 patches to retain at most 10% initial water, temperature ≤50°C, fixed-head tolerances, intact attached hair, dryer off/parked, hands clear, and a 1 s hold; candidate requires ≥98% recovered rigid media, both washers retained, screen supported, and 3 s dwell. Some model calibration remains explicitly missing, but the tested objective is unambiguously unrelated.
comparisons.reason: This is deformable thermal drying and hidden-layer exposure, whereas the candidate is rigid many-body mechanical sieving; generic tool holding or bimanual manipulation does not create overlap.

comparisons.objective: Depress an RJ45 spring latch, withdraw a marked plug from a crowded panel, align and insert it into another port, re-engage the latch, and preserve six neighboring connections; candidate separates loose finishing media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Constrained clip depression, retained withdrawal, cable-obstacle management, precise connector alignment/insertion, and latch engagement versus bimanual screen lifting, agitation, selective aperture transit, and support reseating.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires release before withdrawal, source disconnection, target insertion >8 mm with <1 mm lateral error and <5° angle, hook retention, neighbors undisturbed, and a 2 s released hold; candidate requires mass recovery, washer retention, no spill or invalid passage, supported screen, and a 3 s clear-hand dwell. Connector geometry is approximate, but the rubric is sufficient to distinguish the ability.
comparisons.reason: Crowded connector unlatching and precision reinsertion test constrained mating and latch mechanics, not selective bulk separation through a screen.

comparisons.objective: Disconnect a pneumatic tube safely, isolate and vent pressure, then insert and retention-test a port plug; candidate separates ceramic media from retained washers through a screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: Valve/lock manipulation, collet depression with simultaneous tube extraction, precision plug insertion and pull testing versus bimanual screen lifting, controlled agitation, selective aperture passage and reseating.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires locked and depressurized release, tube clearance, precisely seated/retained plug, safe final valve state and release clearance. Candidate requires ≥98% media recovery, all washers retained, no spill/damage, screen supported, hands ≥60 mm clear and a fresh 3 s dwell.
comparisons.reason: The shared notions of bimanual handling, insertion clearance and released end state are generic. Pneumatic isolation and connector servicing do not test selective many-body separation through physical apertures. No missing rubric detail creates a plausible duplicate.

comparisons.objective: Move the remaining tissue roll to the reserve position, install a refill, close and latch the dispenser, and leave connected tissue accessible; candidate separates loose ceramic media from steel washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Large-roll placement over spindles, spring-lug engagement, cover/panel/latch operation and deformable tissue-tail preservation versus balanced tab grasps, load sharing, orientation-sensitive sifting and controlled reseating.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires correctly seated rolls, shut/bolted cover, correct outlet selection, an attached and measurably accessible tissue edge, settled hardware and robot clearance, with fall/misplacement failures. Candidate instead grades recovered media mass, complete washer retention, spill/damage avoidance, support seating, clearance and 3 s dwell.
comparisons.reason: Both preserve one item while manipulating others, but the tested abilities differ materially: dispenser restocking and deformable-sheet accessibility versus size-selective rigid-body separation through a screen. The available versions provide sufficient thresholds for distinction.

comparisons.objective: Join and positively retain two drive-chain ends using a connecting link, cover plate and spring clips; candidate separates mixed finishing media and washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sub-millimetre coaxial pin/bore alignment, plate placement and spring-clip capture using an applicator versus bimanual load-bearing screen manipulation, controlled tilt/agitation, particle passage and selective retention.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires both pins and bushings seated, cover bores aligned, two clips closed in grooves, chain returned to its guide/cradle, applicator withdrawn, robot clear and a 1 s stable hold. Candidate requires target-media recovery, every washer retained, no loss/damage, screen reseated on both supports, hands clear and a 3 s hold.
comparisons.reason: Chain assembly tests close-tolerance insertion and positive retention; the candidate tests dynamic many-body classification by aperture size. Generic alignment, bimanual coordination and final release do not establish overlap.

comparisons.objective: Hand-mount the final section of a bicycle tire bead into the rim by feeding it into the drop centre without levering beneath it; candidate sifts ceramic media while retaining washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Progressive compliant bead deformation, circumferential feeding, opposing-hand tension/control and rim-channel seating versus rigid screen grasping, load sharing, agitation and selective loose-body passage.
comparisons.success_condition: PR grades bead seating around the rim/drop-centre geometry with tool-use, damage and release constraints; candidate grades recovered media mass, retention of both washers, absence of spill/joint break, support reseating, hand clearance and continuous 3 s stability.
comparisons.reason: The tire task tests compliant closed-loop installation and progressive seating, not selective separation of free rigid bodies through apertures. Their common force control and bimanual coordination are generic primitives, and the supplied spec history is sufficient to distinguish them.

comparisons.objective: Roll puff pastry into a uniformly thin 3–3.2 mm sheet using a spacer-ring rolling pin; candidate separates ceramic finishing media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual rolling-pin grasp, level force application and repeated translational compression of deformable dough versus lifting a rigid screen, controlled orientation/agitation, selective aperture flow and loaded support replacement.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires at least 90% thickness compliance, cross-sheet evenness, pastry remaining on the board, damage limits, and the pin set down and released for a 1 s hold. Candidate requires ≥98% media recovery, all washers retained, no spill/damage, screen supported, hands ≥60 mm clear and a fresh 3 s dwell.
comparisons.reason: Pastry rolling tests distributed deformation and thickness uniformity; the candidate tests granular rigid-body separation and retention. Repeated bimanual motion and final tool release are insufficient for overlap, and the multiple spec versions retain this fundamental distinction.

comparisons.objective: Plant a pepper seedling plug and backfill/firm loose potting mix around it; candidate instead separates ceramic media from retained washers through a screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-2106 requires holding a delicate plug upright while distributing and compacting granular backfill without damaging the plant. Candidate requires bimanual screen grasping, controlled agitation, size-selective aperture passage, washer retention, and support reseating.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-2106 grades plug depth/tilt, four-sided soil level, fill, spill, firmness under a push, release, and plant damage. Candidate grades recovered-media mass, complete washer retention, valid hole passage, reseating on two supports, 60 mm release clearance, and a resettable 3 s dwell.
comparisons.reason: Both manipulate loose bodies and penalize spill, but one tests delicate planting and backfill compaction while the other tests physical size separation through apertures. The detailed rubric versions preserve that substantive distinction.

comparisons.objective: Unhook and remove an air-fryer basket, then place it on a heat-proof mat; candidate separates a mixed charge and returns the screen to its supports.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1814 tests constrained sliding under retaining hooks, handle grasping, lifting, transport, placement, and release. Candidate adds two-tab load sharing and controlled agitation that must pass one object class through apertures while retaining another.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1814 requires the basket on the mat, released with finger clearance, after clearing hooks; earlier versions also cover drawer release and avoiding hot surfaces. Candidate requires at least 98% media recovery for completion credit, all washers retained, no invalid passage or spill, bilateral support, 60 mm clearance, and 3 s stability.
comparisons.reason: Generic container lifting and placement are shared, but PR-1814 does not test selective many-body separation or aperture-mediated retention.

comparisons.objective: Install and correctly tighten a spin-on oil filter; candidate separates ceramic finishing media from steel washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1405 tests coaxial threaded engagement, gasket contact, sustained rotation/regrasping, and controlled final tightening, with versions using either prescribed hand rotation or an 18 N·m wrench endpoint. Candidate tests bimanual screen handling, agitation, selective passage, and reseating.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1405 grades thread engagement, alignment, gasket seating, and a bounded final rotation/torque so the filter is neither loose nor over-tightened. Candidate grades recovery fraction, washer retention, passage history, spill/damage, support contact, release clearance, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: Thread starting and torque-controlled fastening are meaningfully different from separating mixed rigid bodies through a perforated screen.

comparisons.objective: Clamp wooden stock in a screw vise and saw off a 150 mm piece; candidate performs screen separation and recovery.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1984 requires vise clamping, bimanual saw guidance, repeated cutting contact, and dimensional cut control. Candidate requires balanced two-tab lifting, orientation-sensitive agitation, particle passage/retention, and precise screen replacement.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1984 awards partial credit for secure clamping and a full-width groove at least 10 mm deep; full credit needs two physical pieces, retained length 150±1 mm, saw clearance, and limited unintended damage. Candidate instead uses recovered mass, total washer retention, valid aperture transit, no spill/breakage, support/release, and 3 s dwell.
comparisons.reason: Material removal to a dimensional endpoint and selective many-body screening test unrelated physical abilities despite both involving force control.

comparisons.objective: Prepare a moka pot by filling its base below the safety valve, inserting the coffee basket, and fastening the upper chamber; candidate separates ceramic media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR-1506 tests controlled liquid pouring, fill-level regulation, basket insertion, thread alignment, bimanual stabilization, screwing, and regrasping. Candidate tests bimanual screen agitation, real-aperture passage, retention of larger parts, and support reseating.
comparisons.success_condition: PR-1506 requires 122.5–155.8 mL in the base, basket/coffee present, upper chamber straight and snug, limited spill, upright released vessels, and no pot contact; versions refine cross-threading and torque/contact thresholds. Candidate requires ≥98% media recovery for completion credit, every washer retained, no spill or invalid passage, dual support, 60 mm hand clearance, and 3 s dwell.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve loose contents, spill avoidance, bimanual handling, and release, moka-pot assembly does not test size-selective separation through apertures, while the candidate does not test metered pouring, insertion, or threaded fastening.

comparisons.objective: Refit and lock a refrigerator door bin onto two hidden supports; no material separation objective.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual level carrying, tight-clearance alignment, simultaneous support engagement and downward seating, versus controlled sifting of loose bodies through apertures.
comparisons.success_condition: Both bin ends engaged and pushed home, bin level, released and still for 1 s. Candidate instead requires ≥98% media recovery, complete washer retention, two-support reseating, clearance and 3 s dwell. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: Both involve bimanual load sharing and reseating on two supports, but the tested abilities differ meaningfully: precision fixture engagement versus orientation-sensitive selective many-body separation.

comparisons.objective: Thread and close a two-part bent-foot U-lock around a bicycle rim and stand.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rigid-object threading through spokes, angled socket insertion and pivoting latch engagement, not agitation and size-selective aperture passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Lock must link rim and stand, latch at specified seating, be released and stable for 1 s. Candidate grades recovery fraction, washer retention, spill/damage, support placement and 3 s dwell. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: The shared use of two hands and controlled insertion is generic; locking two fixed objects tests topology and latch assembly, not bulk separation through a sieve.

comparisons.objective: Release a camera plate from a cam clamp, clear a retaining lip and transfer it upright to a pad.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cam actuation, constrained extraction and supported payload transfer, versus bimanual screen manipulation with loose-body flow and retention.
comparisons.success_condition: Cam released, payload clear and upright on pad, robot clear and pose stable for 1 s, with drop/fixture guards. Candidate requires quantified separation yield and retained washers before reseating. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: This is release-and-transfer of one captured payload; it does not test selective many-body passage, agitation or simultaneous retained/recovered populations.

comparisons.objective: Depanel a circuit board over a registered break edge and place the freed board in an ESD tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual brace-and-bend fracture with edge registration and post-break handling, rather than load-shared agitation and aperture-based separation.
comparisons.success_condition: A directionally valid break at the edge, board correctly trayed, scrap supported, hands clear and both parts stable for 1 s. Candidate forbids loss/damage and requires mass recovery plus washer retention. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: Although both coordinate two hands and manage multiple resulting bodies, controlled fracture and tray transfer are materially different from nondestructive physical sieving.

comparisons.objective: Rinse selected teeth, evacuate water, then return and release both dental tools.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated liquid delivery, local suction positioning and dual-tool return; candidate manipulates a loaded rigid screen and discrete rigid media.
comparisons.success_condition: Coverage and wet-dwell thresholds, ≥90% liquid recovery, spill/peak-water limits, near-dry mouth, tools returned and released for 1 s. Candidate uses discrete-body mass recovery, washer retention and 3 s support dwell. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: Both concern recovery and spill avoidance, but liquid irrigation/evacuation tests continuous-fluid tool coordination, not size-selective rigid-body screening.

comparisons.objective: Safely assemble a grinding wheel stack on a spindle and verify adequate, non-damaging clamping.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ordered coaxial placement of flanges, blotters and wheel, nut tightening and torque-sensitive verification, not loose-body sifting.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct undamaged wheel and stack, seated nut below the damage limit, successful braked spin and axial tug, hands clear. Candidate instead scores recovery ratio, retained washers and reseated screen dwell. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: The task tests safety-critical serial assembly and torque/clamp control; generic alignment and release do not make it overlap with selective separation.

comparisons.objective: Cut a dead rose cane above an intact bud, retain the offcut and place it in a bin without harming live canes.
comparisons.physical_skill: Target discrimination, secateur operation, bimanual cut-and-catch and delicate offcut transfer, versus screen grasping and controlled agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Cut and final stub 3–15 mm above the bud, bud/live canes intact, offcut never dropped and placed in bin, tool set down and 1 s clearance dwell. Candidate has media-yield and washer-retention criteria. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: Retaining one freed offcut is not equivalent to separating many loose objects by aperture size; the central tested ability is safe precision cutting.

comparisons.objective: Sharpen both faces of a kitchen knife on a whetstone and leave it safely oriented.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained angle and contact-force control during edge-leading strokes with face changes and coverage, not bimanual load sharing or sifting.
comparisons.success_condition: Measured edge sharpness in real trials or qualified bilateral stroke/coverage proxy in simulation, followed by safe released placement and 1 s stability. Candidate requires ≥98% media passage and complete washer retention. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: Repeated controlled motion is only a generic primitive; abrasive edge formation at a constrained angle is a different tested ability from selective screening.

comparisons.objective: Align mating pipe flanges and insert locating pins through corresponding holes.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coaxial flange support, rotational hole alignment and precision pin insertion; candidate requires agitation-driven reorientation and selective passage of many loose bodies.
comparisons.success_condition: Flanges aligned within millimetre/angular tolerances and pins seated in distinct holes; versions differ between four vertical pins and two horizontal pins. Candidate success is separation yield, retention, reseating and dwell. Release requirements are absent in some flange versions but this does not create plausible duplication.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record in generic bimanual support/alignment, yet its tested ability is mating-part registration and insertion, not physical classification through apertures.

comparisons.objective: One-handedly lock a used needle’s hinged sheath against the table and dispose of the syringe in a sharps tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hazard-aware barrel grasping, table-reacted hinge rotation and snap-latch closure, followed by disposal; not bimanual screen agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Sheath catch locked over the needle, unsafe proximity/contact permanently avoided, syringe released in tray and stable for 1 s. Candidate requires selective recovery/retention and 3 s supported dwell. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is one-handed safety-latch actuation under strict needle-clearance constraints, unrelated to sieve-based many-body separation.

comparisons.objective: Close an edge joint between two boards using a ratcheting one-hand bar clamp and leave at least 20 N clamping force.
comparisons.physical_skill: Positioning clamp jaws, pumping a sprung trigger through a one-way drive and force-controlled closure; candidate uses two-tab grasping and loose-body agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Jaws and joint within 0.5 mm, force ≥20 N, boards aligned/level, hands clear and assembly still for 1 s. Earlier versions clamp stacked boards, but none grade separation. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: Both require controlled force and released stability, but ratchet actuation and maintained clamping force test a different mechanism and outcome from selective screening.

comparisons.objective: Inspect and report engine-oil level using a pull–wipe–reseat–reread procedure; candidate separates ceramic media from washers in a screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: Dipstick extraction, rag wiping, reinsertion and visual classification versus bimanual screen lifting, agitation and size-selective aperture passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct oil-level report with cleaned/reseated dipstick and released tools versus ≥98% media recovery, total washer retention, supported screen reseating, release and 3-second dwell. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: The record tests procedural inspection and wiping of one slender instrument, not selective many-body separation through a sieve.

comparisons.objective: Safely rout a curved board edge using a starting pin and bearing; candidate separates mixed finishing media and workpieces.
comparisons.physical_skill: Constrained board pivoting and directional feed around a powered cutter versus bimanual load sharing, controlled screen orientation and particle passage through apertures.
comparisons.success_condition: Specified routed length, safe cutter approach, correct feed direction and board clearance versus media recovery, washer retention, spill prevention, screen support and released dwell. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: Both involve controlled motion, but routing tests hazard-aware workpiece feeding against a cutter rather than physical size separation of loose bodies.

comparisons.objective: Move an untaped-bottom carton of cans to a shelf without losing contents; candidate sifts ceramic media out while deliberately retaining washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous underside support of a failure-prone carton during transport versus controlled bimanual tilting/agitation that induces selective passage while retaining larger rings.
comparisons.success_condition: All cans remain in the carton and the carton is stably released on the shelf versus ≥98% media in the receiver, all washers in the screen, no spill, screen reseated and 3-second release dwell. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: The shared loose-content retention primitive is secondary: one tests supported transport with zero loss, while the candidate tests intentional selective discharge through real apertures.

comparisons.objective: Attach a detachable saucepan handle and use the locked connection to move a pan; candidate separates a mixed batch with a manual screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: Jaw/rim alignment, latching and load-path verification versus bimanual screen grasping, orientation-sensitive sifting and many-body retention.
comparisons.success_condition: Prove retained handle attachment under load, place the pan on a trivet and release versus quantitative media recovery plus washer retention, reseating, clearance and dwell. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: This record tests mechanical attachment followed by load-bearing use, not selective granular separation.

comparisons.objective: Select conveyor parts and assemble a pictured model while rejecting distractors; candidate physically separates ceramic media from washers by size.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed conveyor interception, visual part selection, parking and rigid-part stacking versus bimanual load sharing and force-limited agitation of a loaded perforated screen.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct four-part assembly, all extra parts conveyed away and no belt jam versus ≥98% target-media recovery, complete washer retention, no spill, supported reseating and released dwell. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: Both select among mixed objects, but the conveyor task tests recognition and assembly, whereas the candidate tests physical aperture-based many-body separation.

comparisons.objective: Replace a cartridge in a ratchet-rod dispenser and restore the tool to working configuration; candidate sifts media from retained workpieces.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pawl disengagement, rod retraction, cartridge removal/insertion and re-engagement versus bimanual screen manipulation and size-selective passage of loose bodies.
comparisons.success_condition: Used cartridge collected, replacement aligned and seated, piston/rod/pawl restored, tool cradled and hands released versus media recovery and washer retention with spill/damage gates and 3-second dwell. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: The record tests multi-stage mechanism servicing and insertion, not dynamic separation through apertures.

comparisons.objective: Fit and center a gasket between spread pipe flanges and insert four bolts; candidate separates ceramic media from washers in a screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: Thin-part insertion into a constrained gap, flange preservation and precision bolt placement versus bimanual screen lifting, agitation, selective passage and support replacement.
comparisons.success_condition: Centered flat gasket, undisturbed upper flange, bolts seated through matching holes and released dwell versus ≥98% media recovery, all washers retained, no spill, screen supported and hands clear. No material rubric details are missing.
comparisons.reason: Although both use apertures, the flange task tests precision assembly into specific holes, while the candidate tests many-body size classification by passage through a sieve.

comparisons.objective: Inspect two safety light curtains with test rods and tag the faulty machine.
comparisons.physical_skill: Guide a rod across a sensing field, observe an indicator, and place a tag.
comparisons.success_condition: Both fields are fully tested; only the faulty machine is tagged; rods and hands are clear.
comparisons.reason: The candidate physically separates mixed loose bodies through a sieve and reseats the loaded screen; this record tests sensor inspection and fault-dependent tagging.

comparisons.objective: Swipe a magnetic-stripe card through a reader and return it to its stand.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient a thin card and guide it once through a narrow slot at controlled speed.
comparisons.success_condition: The reader accepts a clean swipe and the released card is upright and still in its stand.
comparisons.reason: Narrow-slot card guidance does not test selective many-body passage, washer retention, bimanual load sharing, or screen reseating.

comparisons.objective: Remove an interrupted suture from a practice pad without damaging the wound.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually lift a knot, place a cutter under the strand, cut flush, and extract it directionally.
comparisons.success_condition: The correct leg is cut near the skin, the stitch is removed toward the wound and deposited, with no pad or wound damage.
comparisons.reason: This is precision cutting and strand extraction; the candidate tests bulk rigid-body separation through apertures and controlled handling of a loaded screen.

comparisons.objective: Install and level a lever set in a bored door.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align concealed spindle/posts, hold two hardware halves seated, and drive screws while maintaining level.
comparisons.success_condition: Both halves are seated, both screws snug, the lever level, and the released assembly stable.
comparisons.reason: Hardware insertion and screw fastening are materially different from selective sifting, retention of oversized parts, and support replacement.

comparisons.objective: Uncap a spray can and coat a plaque while limiting overspray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Remove a cap, hold and actuate a can, and control nozzle aim and coating coverage.
comparisons.success_condition: Required plaque coverage is achieved within the overspray limit, with the cap parked and can safely stabilized.
comparisons.reason: Coating deposition and overspray control do not test physical size-based separation of loose bodies through a screen.

comparisons.objective: Serve a drink through a self-closing drive-thru window.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a spring-loaded slider while transporting and placing a cup, then withdraw before closure.
comparisons.success_condition: The cup is upright on the outer shelf, both arms are inside, and the window closes without contact or cup damage.
comparisons.reason: Although bimanual load coordination appears in both, this record tests constrained handoff through a closing barrier, not selective many-body sieving or screen reseating.

comparisons.objective: Scribe a shelf end to match an uneven wall.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize a shelf while tracing a wall profile continuously with a pencil compass.
comparisons.success_condition: A continuous, accurate non-straight profile is marked and the tool is released clear without moving or dropping the shelf.
comparisons.reason: Surface-guided profile tracing is a different tested ability from agitation-driven aperture passage and simultaneous retention of larger workpieces.

comparisons.objective: Fill and remove a blood tube from a needle already placed in a training arm.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize the needle holder while inserting, filling, extracting, and placing a collection tube.
comparisons.success_condition: The tube is filled, removed, and released in its tray without excessive needle translation, lateral motion, pivoting, or holder release.
comparisons.reason: This record tests delicate insertion/extraction under needle-stability constraints; the candidate tests selective loose-body separation and loaded screen manipulation.

comparisons.objective: Prove a voltage detector before and after testing a bar, abstaining if proof fails.
comparisons.physical_skill: Balance and position a stick-mounted detector, operate buttons, interpret proof feedback, and execute a conditional test.
comparisons.success_condition: On a working tester the detector completes prove-test-prove and is laid down clear; on a failed tester the bar is never touched.
comparisons.reason: Conditional electrical-safety inspection and long-tool placement do not exercise sieve agitation, aperture passage, retained-part control, or screen support alignment.

comparisons.objective: Carry hot tea to a coaster without passing over or contacting a person's arm.
comparisons.physical_skill: Transport and place a filled cup while maintaining uprightness and obstacle clearance.
comparisons.success_condition: The cup rests upright and still on the coaster with no spill, impact, unsafe over-arm path, or robot contact.
comparisons.reason: Safe liquid transport around a moving obstacle differs from bimanual selective separation of mixed rigid bodies through physical openings.

comparisons.objective: Release a cordless-drill battery and place it in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize the drill, depress two release buttons together, slide the pack off its rail, and place it.
comparisons.success_condition: The released pack is fully removed, let go, resting still inside the tray, while the drill remains controlled.
comparisons.reason: A latched-component removal task does not test many-body sifting, orientation-dependent aperture passage, washer retention, or reseating a loaded screen.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates ceramic media from retained washers through a screen; pr-1151 purges air from a syringe while preserving liquid and returns it to a rack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests bimanual load sharing, controlled sieve agitation, selective aperture passage, and reseating; pr-1151 tests syringe reorientation, barrel stabilization, precise plunger advancement, and fluid-loss control. Shared careful handling and re-racking are generic.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades recovered media mass, complete washer retention, support seating, 60 mm release, and a 3 s dwell with spill/damage gates; pr-1151 grades residual air and sample loss plus syringe pose, release, and a 1 s hold. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: The tested transformation—many-body size separation through physical apertures—is meaningfully different from controlled air expulsion through a syringe.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates mixed loose bodies with a manual screen; pr-1775 reinstalls a loaded drawer on roller slides and pull-tests its engagement.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires bimanual screen grasping, tilting/agitation, selective retention, and support replacement; pr-1775 requires carrying a loaded drawer above hook-clearance height, aligning both runners, closing, releasing, and reopening. Shared bimanual carrying and reseating are generic.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires at least 98% target recovery for completion, both washers retained, both supports engaged, hands clear, and 3 s stability; pr-1775 requires slide engagement, closure with hands off, then 30–80 mm reopening, with load loss or a fall scoring zero. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Installing and verifying constrained drawer-slide engagement does not test selective particle passage or agitation of loose contents.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates ceramic media from steel washers; pr-1891 seats an add-on PCB onto two rows of header pins without bending them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests bimanual load sharing and orientation-sensitive sifting through many apertures; pr-1891 tests fine angular alignment and even force-controlled insertion of a tilted board onto pins. Both demand controlled orientation, but the contact mechanics and manipulation goal differ.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades recovery fraction, washer retention, support replacement, release, and spill/damage history; pr-1891 grades leveling, insertion depth, absence of pin bending, full seating, release, and a 1 s hold. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Selective many-body separation is not equivalent to tolerance-sensitive rigid-part alignment and press-fit insertion.

comparisons.objective: Candidate performs screen separation and returns the screen to supports; pr-1912 seats an ear-thermometer probe, triggers a reading, holds it still, and lays it down.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests bimanual grasp/load sharing, agitation, loose-body retention, and reseating; pr-1912 tests single-tool pose alignment to an anatomical canal, button actuation, and submillimetric steady holding. Shared placement and release are generic.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires recovered-media mass, all washers retained, no spill or break, supported screen, 60 mm clearance, and 3 s dwell; pr-1912 requires valid probe seating, a completed 3 s measurement, safe insertion depth, laying down, and a 1 s final hold. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Probe alignment and motionless measurement do not exercise selective aperture passage or controlled agitation of mixed rigid bodies.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates two classes of loose production bodies through a screen; pr-1930 removes and replaces two thin shelf-edge price tickets.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires bimanual screen handling, controlled agitation, and simultaneous pass/retain behavior; pr-1930 requires opening a sprung strip, extracting and inserting thin cards, correct assignment, and avoiding nearby cans. Shared bimanual coordination is generic.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades mass recovery and complete washer retention before support replacement and release; pr-1930 awards per-ticket removal and correct insertion, requires the untouched ticket to remain seated, hands withdrawn, and a long stable dwell, with can tipping as permanent zero. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Thin-card extraction/insertion under a sprung cover is a different dexterous ability from physical size separation through a sieve.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates ceramic media from washers by screening; pr-2101 empties four concentrate bottles into a filling tank and closes a valve at the target level.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests bimanual screen grasping, load sharing, limited agitation, selective retention, and reseating; pr-2101 tests repeated bottle grasping and pouring plus timing a quarter-turn valve. Tilting containers while preventing spill is shared, but selective aperture separation is not.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades recovered target mass, zero washer passage, support seating, release, and 3 s dwell, with any spill invalidating the trial; pr-2101 grades emptied bottles and final liquid level with the valve shut, with overflow, spill, bottle loss, or tank movement scoring zero. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Despite shared tilt and spill control, pr-2101 tests liquid transfer and fill-level timing, not pass-versus-retain separation of mixed rigid bodies.

comparisons.objective: Candidate screens ceramic media away from retained washers; pr-1288 selects and mounts a matching driver bit, power-tightens a drawer knob, load-tests it, and returns the tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires bimanual support of a loose-body screen, controlled agitation, and accurate reseating; pr-1288 requires bit selection and insertion, tool-to-screw alignment, powered axial feed, drawer stabilization, and tool return. Shared tool handling and release are generic.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate uses recovery mass plus washer-retention, spill, support, clearance, and dwell checks; pr-1288 requires stable bit installation, at least 1.3 mm powered screw feed, knob closure, a 5 N hold test, and stable tool return. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Powered fastening with removable-tool assembly and load verification does not test selective many-body screening.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates mixed rigid media using a manual screen; pr-1454 loads a caulking gun and lays a continuous sealant bead along a bath joint.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests bimanual load sharing, controlled tilt/agitation, particle passage and retention, then support replacement; pr-1454 tests release-lever/rod coordination, cartridge insertion, trigger-driven extrusion, and continuous nozzle path following. Shared bimanual tool handling is generic.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades recovered-media mass and total washer retention with spill/damage gates, support seating, release, and 3 s dwell; pr-1454 grades loaded-gun state, sealed joint coverage and gap size, mess limits, and putting the gun down. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Continuous material deposition along a joint is mechanically and outcome-wise different from selective separation through apertures.

comparisons.objective: Candidate separates ceramic finishing media from steel washers; pr-1570 adjusts a wrench jaw, loosens a nut in the safe direction, removes the wrench, and sets it down.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate requires bimanual screen control, agitation, many-body retention/pass-through behavior, and reseating; pr-1570 requires fine worm adjustment, correct fixed-jaw loading, torque application, and tool removal. Shared grasping and set-down are generic.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate grades recovered mass, washer retention, no spill or break, support seating, release clearance, and dwell; pr-1570 grades nut rotation and wrench set-down while permanently rejecting loose-jaw or wrong-direction pulls. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Adjustable-wrench fitting and torque application do not test bulk selective separation or loose-body dynamics.

comparisons.objective: Candidate screens ceramic media away from retained washers; pr-2031 aseptically spikes an IV bag and primes its drip chamber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Candidate tests bimanual screen grasping, controlled agitation, pass/retain selectivity, and loaded reseating; pr-2031 tests cap removal without sterile-interface contact, spike alignment/insertion, chamber orientation, and calibrated squeeze/release priming. Shared bimanual coordination and liquid-loss caution are generic.
comparisons.success_condition: Candidate requires at least 98% recovery for completion, every washer retained, no spill or tunneling, both supports engaged, hands clear, and 3 s dwell; pr-2031 requires both caps removed, 23–25 mm spike seating, 15–27 mm fill height, no contamination or overfill, release, and 1 s rest. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparisons.reason: Aseptic insertion and drip-chamber priming test sterile-interface handling and fluid metering, not selective rigid-body screening.

comparisons.objective: Refit and retain a mixer beater and guard, raise the bowl, then verify powered start/stop; candidate separates loose media from washers through a screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bayonet insertion, guard placement, lever/button operation, and powered-equipment clearance versus bimanual screen lifting, load sharing, controlled agitation, and selective aperture passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Beater/guard retention, raised bowl, prescribed rotation, stopped mechanism, and clear hands versus ≥98% media recovery, total washer retention, supported screen, release, and 3-second dwell.
comparisons.reason: Both involve bimanual equipment handling, but they test different mechanisms and outcomes. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Guide a plasma torch along a straightedge to sever plate and drop an offcut; candidate physically sieves a mixed loose-body load.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual straightedge stabilization and speed-controlled cutting versus two-tab load sharing, orientation-sensitive sifting, and spill-limited agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Sound cut segments, free offcut, safe clearance, and returned tools versus recovered media fraction, retained washers, reseated screen, release, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: Shared bimanual force control is generic; cutting quality and material separation through apertures are meaningfully different tested abilities. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Mount one shaft between fixed and sprung bench centres; candidate separates ceramic media from steel washers in a supported screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a release lever while aligning two shaft centre holes versus symmetric tab grasping, dynamic loose-load control, agitation, and screen replacement.
comparisons.success_condition: Both points seated, lever at rest, shaft still and released versus target recovery, washer retention, no spill, dual support, hand clearance, and 3-second dwell.
comparisons.reason: The record tests constrained precision seating into opposed centres, not selective many-body passage. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Place three personal devices on matching charging interfaces; candidate performs physical size-selective separation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Device-specific placement, magnetic alignment, and strap handling versus bimanual lifting and controlled agitation of a loaded perforated screen.
comparisons.success_condition: Released charging with visible feedback for five seconds and limited stand motion versus ≥98% media recovery with all washers retained and the screen reseated.
comparisons.reason: Both require stable released endpoints, but functional charging alignment does not test loose-body separation. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Seat a Mini-ITX board onto four standoffs with its ports aligned; candidate sifts mixed finishing media and workpieces.
comparisons.physical_skill: Planar multi-pin alignment and fragile-board placement versus bimanual load sharing, tilting/agitation, particle passage, and retention control.
comparisons.success_condition: Four holes seated, I/O aligned, board still and hands clear versus recovery ratio, washer retention, support contact, release, and dwell with hard spill/damage failures.
comparisons.reason: Multi-point component seating and selective many-body screening have different physical constraints and observable outcomes. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Remove each gnocchi from water after it floats and plate it; candidate separates ceramic media from retained washers through screen apertures.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed slotted-spoon scooping of individual soft pieces and burner operation versus bimanual screen grasping, whole-load agitation, aperture orientation, and simultaneous retention.
comparisons.success_condition: Count of timely plated pieces, no finger contact, burner off versus mass recovery fraction, every washer retained, no spill, screen supported, and released dwell.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest perforated-tool record, but it tests event-timed individual retrieval from liquid rather than size-selective bulk passage through a manipulated screen. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Insert, centre, and tighten a drill bit with a keyed chuck; candidate performs bulk media/workpiece separation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-axis insertion, key-pinion engagement, torque buildup, and regrasping versus two-handed screen lifting, orientation control, agitation, and loose-load management.
comparisons.success_condition: Bit captured, centred, torque-secure, key removed, drill still and hands clear versus high media recovery, washer retention, screen support, clearance, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: The common need for force control is generic; keyed rotational clamping is not the candidate’s tested ability. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Dial and open a hanging combination padlock; candidate separates a mixed industrial load through a sieve.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential dial rotation with rim regrasping on a swinging body, followed by shackle pull, versus bimanual load sharing and controlled sifting.
comparisons.success_condition: Wheel gates set, shackle open on hasp, lock released and still versus recovered media, retained washers, reseated screen, clear hands, and continuous dwell.
comparisons.reason: Stateful dial manipulation and bulk physical screening have no meaningful task-level overlap beyond generic grasping. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Unfold and configure a laptop stand with two rods in highest slots; candidate separates loose media from retained washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Scissor-linkage deployment and dual rod-slot seating versus lifting and agitating a loaded screen while controlling passage and retention.
comparisons.success_condition: Full spread, both rods seated, stand contained, stable and released versus recovery ratio, no washer loss or spill, dual support, release, and 3-second dwell.
comparisons.reason: Both use two hands and finish on supports, but linkage configuration does not test selective many-body separation. Missing rubric details: none material in the final spec.

comparisons.objective: Carry four filled glasses into a bus tub in one trip; candidate separates finishing media from washers and returns the screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: Multi-object pinch carrying while keeping hollow tumblers upright and contents contained versus bilateral screen grasp, controlled tilt/agitation, selective passage, and reseating.
comparisons.success_condition: Four upright delivered glasses with ice/straws retained, one trip, release and stillness versus ≥98% media recovery, all washers retained, no spill, supported screen and dwell.
comparisons.reason: Both penalize content loss, but carrying intact containers and screening intermixed free bodies test different abilities; the one-trip constraint is not candidate-relevant. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Cap four pens with matching caps and sort them by color; candidate physically separates media and washers by aperture size.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated small-part cap insertion and planar sorting versus bimanual loaded-screen handling, force-limited agitation, and geometry-dependent passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct cap retention and color-area placement after release versus recovered target mass, retained washers, no spill, screen support, clearance, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: The candidate’s separation is physical and many-body, not semantic color sorting or repeated insertion. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Strip a measured length of cable insulation in a lever-operated station; candidate screens ceramic media from steel workpieces.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cable insertion, coordinated lever hold, resisted withdrawal, and release versus dual-tab grasping, load sharing, tilting/agitation, and screen reseating.
comparisons.success_condition: 8–12 mm stripped with lever raised and hands clear versus ≥98% media recovered, washers retained, no spill/damage, screen supported, and 3-second dwell.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual coordination is shared only at a generic level; resisted stripping and selective screening are different physical mechanisms. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Stretch an O-ring over threads and seat it untwisted in a groove; candidate separates rigid loose bodies through apertures.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compliant-ring stretching, deformation control, and circumferential seating versus rigid screen manipulation, dynamic load control, agitation, and size selection.
comparisons.success_condition: Ring fully seated without excessive stretch or twist and released versus media recovery, washer retention, spill prevention, screen support, clearance, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: The record is a deformable seal-installation task; the candidate is rigid many-body separation. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Replace a toilet roll on a spring spindle and seat both spindle ends; candidate sifts an industrial media/workpiece mixture.
comparisons.physical_skill: Spindle compression, roll loading, and hidden-end socket alignment versus bilateral screen grasp, changing-load stabilization, controlled agitation, and reseating.
comparisons.success_condition: New roll mounted, both ends seated, empty tube removed, release and stillness versus recovery/retention thresholds, no spill, dual support, clearance, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: Both require bimanual support replacement, but spring-spindle insertion does not exercise selective aperture passage or loose-load control. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Mix flour and liquid into dough while stabilizing a loose bowl; candidate separates ceramic media from washers using a screen.
comparisons.physical_skill: One-hand bowl stabilization plus spoon-driven mixing of particulate/liquid material versus two-hand screen load sharing, lifting, tilting/agitation, and selective passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Fraction of flour mixed, with bowl-tip and spill failures versus fraction of media recovered, complete washer retention, supported screen, release, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: Both manipulate many-body contents and penalize spills, but homogenization in a bowl is the opposite physical outcome from geometry-selective separation. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Raise a hanging photo and spring-clip its free corner to a wire; candidate separates a loose industrial mixture.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual support of a flexible sheet plus peg squeezing and precise clip placement versus rigid screen load sharing and controlled agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Second peg closes on wire and photo, photo level, released and still versus media recovery, washer retention, supported screen, hand clearance, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: Flexible-sheet support and spring clipping are unrelated to selective rigid-body screening. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Use a plunger to clear a basin blockage and restore drainage; candidate sieves finishing media from retained steel washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cup sealing and cyclic pressure/flow generation versus dual-tab lifting, orientation-sensitive agitation, and selective solid passage through apertures.
comparisons.success_condition: Specified drained volume, clear pipe bore, limited spill/damage, plunger clear versus target recovery fraction, washer retention, screen support, release, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: Both involve passage through openings, but hydraulic obstruction removal is not bulk size separation or loaded-screen manipulation. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Load, uncap, recap, and cock a pen lancing device; candidate separates loose media and workpieces.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-part insertion, twist-off fracture, snap fitting, sprung sliding, and needle avoidance versus bimanual screen handling and controlled many-body agitation.
comparisons.success_condition: Lancet home, tab removed, cap secured, device cocked, safely released versus recovery/retention, no spill or damage, screen reseating, clearance, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: The record tests a multi-fit device procedure with a sharp-part hazard, not physical screening. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Roll a mailer end panel and seat two hidden tabs into base holes; candidate separates finishing media from washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a sprung wall while forming a double crease and blindly inserting two tabs versus bilateral screen grasp, loose-load control, agitation, and support replacement.
comparisons.success_condition: Both tabs seated, wall square/flat, no crushing or excess box motion, released stillness versus media recovery, washer retention, no spill, supported screen, clearance, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: Both demand bimanual stabilization, but carton folding/tab insertion and selective many-body sifting are meaningfully different. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Fit a long server bezel by seating right tabs and engaging a left spring latch; candidate screens ceramic media from steel washers.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual long-part alignment, asymmetric hook-and-pivot insertion, and latch force control versus symmetric tab load sharing, screen tilting/agitation, and particle retention.
comparisons.success_condition: Tabs seated, bezel flush, latch overlapped, low force and released rest versus recovery fraction, all washers retained, no spill/damage, dual support, clearance, and dwell.
comparisons.reason: Both include tabs and bimanual handling, but the tabs serve different functions: bezel attachment versus grasp points for dynamic selective separation. Missing rubric details: none material.

comparisons.objective: Calibrate a colorimeter with a blank, measure a sample at a requested wavelength, and return both cuvettes.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient and insert individual cuvettes, operate buttons and a sliding hood, and perform reference-dependent instrument sequencing.
comparisons.success_condition: A valid calibrated measurement record plus both cuvettes released in separate rack pockets; loss forces zero.
comparisons.reason: The candidate tests bimanual many-body size separation through apertures, not instrument calibration or precision cuvette handling. No material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Thread a deformable shock cord through a spring cord lock while holding its plunger open.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained spring compression combined with deformable threading through a tight passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Cord passes through with at least 40 mm on each side, the spring grips it, and lock and cord are released and still.
comparisons.reason: Both involve bimanual coordination, but deformable threading under spring load is meaningfully different from agitating a rigid screen to selectively separate loose bodies. No material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Install a rack-server air shroud by engaging two tabs beneath a fan cage and seating the shroud.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual transport, tilt-sensitive dual-tab insertion, and constrained lowering around server components.
comparisons.success_condition: Both tabs are inserted at least 3 mm, all four corners are seated within 2 mm, and the shroud is released and still.
comparisons.reason: Dual-tab insertion and seating test assembly alignment, whereas the candidate tests selective particle passage and retention during controlled agitation. No material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Measure tyre tread depth with a pen gauge and return the gauge to its rest.
comparisons.physical_skill: Precisely seat a probe on a groove floor with its foot spanning adjacent ribs, then withdraw without changing the reading.
comparisons.success_condition: A valid reading within 0.8 mm of true depth after verified seating, followed by release on the gauge rest.
comparisons.reason: This is localized metrology and probe contact, not bimanual load sharing or many-body separation through a screen. No material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Expose and scan a barcode on a limp training arm, then restore the arm and scanner.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a sprung forearm rotated while the other hand aims and triggers a scanner within its optical envelope.
comparisons.success_condition: A valid scan without excessive arm speed, followed by the scanner on the table and forearm returned palm-down.
comparisons.reason: Its core ability is sustained limb positioning plus optical instrument use, not orientation-controlled sifting and selective retention. No material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Secure a housing in a rollover fixture, invert and lock it, then install a wear pad.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential fixture loading, retention-bar operation, controlled inversion, bolt actuation, and pad insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Housing secured and inverted, bolt home, pad seated, all parts retained, and both hands clear while still.
comparisons.reason: Although both manipulate a supported object bimanually and finish released, fixture inversion and component installation do not test loose-body aperture separation. No material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Reattach a detached live wrist camera to its native mount and release it secured.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cross-arm precision alignment, tapered-channel insertion, latch engagement, and sensor restoration.
comparisons.success_condition: Camera aligned and latched with advancing live frames for two seconds after the inserting hand clears; dropping invalidates credit.
comparisons.reason: This tests precision insertion and latching of one component, not controlled agitation that separates one loose-body class while retaining another. Earlier binary rubrics lacked partial-credit detail, but later versions resolve it and the distinction is clear.

comparisons.objective: Seat an oil-feed sleeve while registering its radial hole with the housing passage.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sub-millimetre cylindrical insertion with preserved angular orientation and unobstructed port alignment.
comparisons.success_condition: Released, supported seating for one second with the complete 10 mm passage unobstructed for full credit.
comparisons.reason: Port-registration insertion is a single-part assembly ability, unlike bimanual screening based on physical size and many-body dynamics. No material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Remove a drawer by actuating opposite-sense slide releases, then set it down.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated bilateral release actuation while pulling a bulky drawer off two slides, followed by controlled placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Drawer fully clears both slides, lies flat and still on the table, and both grippers remain at least 30 mm clear.
comparisons.reason: The shared need for two-hand coordination does not equate opposite latch release and extraction with selective loose-body sifting. No material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Secure a carton to a luggage cart using a stretched bungee with one hook on each frame tube.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual hook placement against elastic tension and load stabilization under a subsequent cart-motion test.
comparisons.success_condition: Both hooks remain home, the cord restrains the carton, and the carton survives tilt, rock, lift, and tip testing after release.
comparisons.reason: Elastic hook placement and restraint under external motion test a different ability from grasping a rigid screen and inducing selective aperture passage. No material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Dispose of a used procedure tray while first securing an exposed needle in a sharps container.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hazard-aware sequencing and safe handling of a syringe, tray, and forceps without needle contact.
comparisons.success_condition: Syringe wholly in the sharps container and tray and forceps in waste, released and still; unsafe contact, loss, or syringe disposal in waste permanently scores zero.
comparisons.reason: This tests safety-aware object routing and sharp avoidance, not physical size separation through a screen. No material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Measure a burger patty's internal temperature by probing through its side to the centre.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize a compliant food item with a turner while inserting a slender probe at controlled height, angle, and depth.
comparisons.success_condition: Valid centre reading without breakout or excessive patty motion, followed by withdrawal, tool placement, release, and stillness.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual stabilization and probing are different from shared-load screen manipulation and selective many-body recovery. No material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Snap a specimen swab at its breakpoint while its tip remains in a free-standing transport tube, then discard the handle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Brace a light tube while applying controlled bending force to break a slender shaft at a designated point.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct in-tube break, handle in waste cup, tube upright with tip retained, all objects still, and grippers clear; spill or tip removal scores zero.
comparisons.reason: Controlled breakage while stabilizing a container does not test aperture-based separation or retention of mixed loose rigid bodies. No material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Load a thin card under a clipboard clip, square and against its stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a spring lever open with one hand while friction-sliding and aligning a thin sheet with the other.
comparisons.success_condition: Card is spring-clamped, aligned and fully inserted, survives a 60-degree board tilt with at most 3 mm slip, and both hands are clear.
comparisons.reason: The common bimanual asymmetry is generic; spring actuation plus sheet sliding is not selective sifting under changing loose-body load. No material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Capture a reference angle with a bevel gauge, transfer it to a board, and draw the corresponding line.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fit and preserve a passive hinge angle during transport, seat the gauge, and guide a marker accurately.
comparisons.success_condition: Valid retained angle transfer plus a single line meeting coverage, angle, gap, stray-mark, and final-clearance thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Angle capture and guided marking test metrology and tool use, not controlled many-body separation through physical apertures. No material rubric details are missing.

comparisons.objective: Scrape adhered griddle debris over the plate lip into its grease tray without scattering or gouging.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain scraper-edge contact and angle, break adhered residue free, overlap strokes, and push fragments into a receiver.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 98% of debris reaches the tray with minimal residue and loss, no damaging gouge, and the scraper is released and still.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest record because both recover many pieces into a receiver and penalize spill, but scraping adhered residue with a tool does not test size-selective aperture passage while retaining larger workpieces in a lifted screen.
